findings: Milne equation7.3.1 is an arithmetic identity derived by duality and Euler characteristic. The BSD-invariance theorem heading is not used as an assumption of the BSD leading-term equality. Finite Sha and the actual dual principally polarized isogenies remain explicit incoming hypotheses.

With z=ker/coker, the rational-point ratio is (tors_A/tors_B)^2 J/I. The finite Sha dual pairing supplies Sha_B/Sha_A. With IJ=2 and height functoriality, J/I=Reg_B/Reg_A=2/I². This yields precisely the stated orientation for s_A-s_B.

Milne initially uses the pullback differential. Replacing it by separately chosen global Neron generators retains the |a|_v factors, whose global product is one. Real change of variables includes kernel/cokernel; the dimension-two cotangent relation ab=4 is distinct from rank-one IJ=2. The application does not discard component factors or invoke a leading-term identity.

At an odd companion prime with good E0 and tame totally ramified quadratic extension, n2 satisfies the root-of-unity and invertibility hypotheses. Edixhoven gives a functorial residue-field filtration with connected positive part and fixed good fibre E0[2]. Since2 is invertible this is finite etale, so the component identification preserves Frobenius. Its rational count is #E[2]^Frob, equal to4 only under the actual full rational2-torsion hypothesis.

Proposition4.1 and the pre-invariants filtration5.1 give the Neron model of the Weil restriction and its connected special fibre: a good elliptic quotient with vector kernel. This is not the fixed subgroup used for the twist. The positive component-ratio valuation enters with negative sign in the determinant expression containing -s_A.
